name: add_job
description: Add a job application to JobSync. Resolves or creates company, job title, location, and source by name. Returns a transparency report of what was matched vs. created.

jobDescription.description: The complete job posting text, copied in full — do not summarize, shorten, or paraphrase it. Markdown-formatted is supported; plain text also works. Use 'N/A' only if no description is available at all.

location.description: City, province/state, country, or 'Remote' — e.g. 'Calgary, AB'. Do not include a street address.

source.description: Job board or site the listing came from, e.g. 'LinkedIn', 'Indeed', 'company website'. If not stated explicitly, infer it from the job posting's URL/domain when possible instead of leaving it blank.

workplaceType.description: Work arrangement stated in the posting. One of: Remote, Hybrid, Onsite.

status.description: Application status. One of: new, draft, applied, interview, offer, offer-accepted, offer-declined, rejected, expired, archived, withdrawn. Defaults to 'draft'.

dueDate.description: Application deadline as an ISO-8601 datetime string. Defaults to 3 days from now if omitted.

applied.description: Set true if you have already submitted the application

appliedDate.description: Date the application was submitted as an ISO-8601 datetime string

jobUrl.description: Direct URL to the job posting

salaryRange.description: Salary range as a free-form string, e.g. '$120k–$150k' or '100,000 CAD'

tags.description: Skills required for the job (max 10 applied, extras are dropped). Tags are created if they don't exist. e.g. ['React', 'TypeScript', 'Node.js']

allowDuplicate.description: Force-create even if a matching job already exists. Prefer upsert:true for re-runs of the same search; use this only for a genuinely different posting.

upsert.description: If this posting is already saved, update it with the fields supplied here instead of reporting a duplicate. A posting counts as already saved when it matches on URL, or on company+title within the dedupe window — so this works for postings with no URL at all. Set this on every re-run of a saved or scheduled search, whether or not you have a URL.

name: find_job
description: Look up whether a job posting is already saved in JobSync, by URL. Call this before add_job when re-running a search. With no URL to look up, use add_job's upsert instead of skipping dedupe.

jobUrl.description: Direct URL to the job posting. Matched against saved jobs using the same canonical key as add_job's duplicate detection, so tracking parameters and host casing don't matter.

name: update_job
description: Correct or enrich a job previously added through MCP. Only the fields you supply change. Supplying a fuller jobDescription re-classifies the posting and requests a fresh match analysis — use this instead of re-adding with allowDuplicate.

jobId.description: The id of the job to update, as returned by add_job or find_job. Only jobs created through MCP can be updated.

jobDescription.description: The complete job posting text, copied in full — do not summarize. Supplying this re-classifies the job's description completeness and, if it is now substantive enough, a fresh match analysis is requested.

workplaceType.description: Work arrangement stated in the posting. One of: Remote, Hybrid, Onsite.

status.description: Application status. One of: new, draft, applied, interview, offer, offer-accepted, offer-declined, rejected, expired, archived, withdrawn.

tags.description: Skills required for the job, e.g. ['React', 'TypeScript']. Replaces the job's existing tags wholesale rather than merging, so include the tags returned by find_job that should be kept (max 10 applied).

name: add_question
description: Add an entry to the Question Bank. Resolves or creates tags by name. Returns a transparency report of what was matched vs. created.

answer.description: Markdown-formatted answer/notes (required). Plain text also works.

tags.description: Skill/topic tags (max 10 applied, extras dropped). Created if they don't exist.

name: save_match_result
description: Persist a job-fit match analysis (produced by you, the agent) against a job previously created with add_job. Call this after add_job hands you a match directive.

jobId.description: The id of the job returned by add_job.

resumeId.description: The id of the resume this match was scored against, exactly as given in the add_job directive. Omit only if the directive had none.

matchText.description: Your full match analysis: a leading 'SCORES: match=<0-100> recommendation=<strong|good|partial|weak>' line, then a markdown body.

name: add_jobs_batch
description: Add several jobs in one call. Same per-item behaviour as add_job (including upsert and the match directive); returns one labelled result per item. Use this for scheduled runs instead of N sequential add_job calls.

jobs.description: Up to 10 jobs, each with the same fields as add_job. Processed in order; each item consumes one unit of the MCP rate-limit budget.

name: save_match_results_batch
description: Persist several job-fit match analyses in one call. Same per-item behaviour as save_match_result; returns one labelled result per item.

jobId.description: The id of the job returned by add_job.

resumeId.description: The id of the resume this match was scored against, exactly as given in the add_job directive. Omit only if the directive had none.

results.description: Up to 10 match analyses, each with the same fields as save_match_result.

name: review_resume
description: Fetch the user's default resume so you can review it. Returns the normalized resume text plus a directive — produce the review yourself, then call save_resume_review with the result.

name: save_resume_review
description: Persist a resume review (produced by you, the agent) against the resume previously handed to you by review_resume. Call this after review_resume hands you a review directive.

resumeId.description: The id of the resume this review was produced for, exactly as given in the review_resume directive.

reviewText.description: Your full resume review: a leading 'SCORES: overall=<0-100> impact=<0-100> clarity=<0-100> ats=<0-100>' line, then a markdown body.
